topics: KV cache and prefix caching potential
transcript:
Meeting header: 2027-08-02 14:00 PT — Duration: ~52m — Attendees: Avery Chen (Redwood AE), Marcus Patel (Redwood SE), Sofia Alvarez (Redwood CSM), Janelle Morris (NexaCart Head of ML), Rajesh Iyer (CTO), Liam O'Connor (Platform Lead), Priya Singh (SRE)

[00:00] Avery Chen: hey everyone, thanks for joining — um it's a QBR/check-in style but i wanted to kick off with runway and reliability stuff first, hope that's OK.
[00:12] Janelle Morris: yeah that's perfect, we've got 20 minutes to go over adoption signals and then tag into reliability stuff, perfect.
[00:18] Marcus Patel: quick note, i'll surface the microbenchmark plan then show a couple of config levers — batching, kv cache, and routing policies — that usually move the needle.
[00:30] Rajesh Iyer: before we start — we had a big promo last month, spikes in latency, some 95th pct outliers up to 1.8s on the checkout flow, that cost us conversions. want to understand what redwood saw on your side and options.
[00:44] Sofia Alvarez: noted, we pulled session traces — Marcus will share a small playback of patterns. also we'll propose a 30/60/90 runway with cost impact.
[00:52] Liam O'Connor: our stack is nodejs -> internal gateway -> redwood hosted API. we don't use VPC today; everything is public. exploring dedicated or vpc for isolation.
[01:05] Marcus Patel: sounds good. the reason you saw spikes likely is correlated to very short bursts with long context windows — customers including NexaCart tend to send cart history + product embeddings which increases sequence length. in-hosted mode the autoscaler may create cold-start bumps.
[01:25] Janelle Morris: to be clear, we compress history client-side but still send ~1.2k tokens on checkout sometimes.
[01:32] Marcus Patel: okay that explains kernel switching overhead — when sequence lengths jump the runtime picks different kernel paths. we can mitigate via two options: dedicated capacity pinned to your workload (eliminates cold resource switches) or workload-aware routing with a lower-capacity but tuned model variant for bursts.
[01:48] Rajesh Iyer: can you spell out the econ tradeoff — dedicated nodes vs route-to-cheaper-sim model? our CFO is sensitive to monthly committed spend.
[01:57] Avery Chen: yes — dedicated is predictable cost, better 95th latency and isolation; hosting with smart routing is variable but can be cheaper if you tolerate occasional tail increases. we'll share model: committed monthly vs expected per-token with burst premiums.
[02:12] Priya Singh: also need to confirm SOC2 audit and KMS usage. if we go dedicated or private, key management must be customer-managed.
[02:22] Sofia Alvarez: noted — we have SOC2 Type II and KMS integrations; Marcus will send security doc links after the call.
[02:30] Marcus Patel: ok i'll open my laptop — the microbenchmark plan: we'll replay 48 hours of your traffic with synthetic promo bursts, compare three configs: hosted-default, hosted-with-prefix-cache, and dedicated-minimum. goal is measure p50/p95/p99 and cost per 1k requests. plan to run week of 8/9 if you approve.
[02:52] Janelle Morris: approve. also, can we include a routing policy that falls back to a quantized variant during bursts? we've seen quality regressions before.
[03:03] Marcus Patel: yes — we'll include a quantized-compatible variant and report BLEU-style similarity metrics for outputs on your prompt set. note: quantization may reduce memory and cost but may slightly alter outputs; we'll flag regressions.
[03:18] Liam O'Connor: do you support prefix caching for the shopping session? could cache product descriptions and only send diffs.
[03:26] Marcus Patel: absolutely — automatic prefix/KV caching is a recommended lever. with NexaCart patterns, we expect 20-40% token reduction on average for checkout flows. depends on freshness requirements.
[03:38] Rajesh Iyer: what about model rollouts — we want canary then rapid rollback if quality dips.
[03:44] Avery Chen: Redwood Console supports canary and A/B rollouts with automatic fallback. we'll demo the runbook in the follow-up.
[03:53] Priya Singh: security: if we move to VPC/private deployment we'll need audit logs, SAML SSO, and support for HSM/KMS. what's the timeline for that?
[04:05] Sofia Alvarez: typical timeline is 4–8 weeks for a VPC onboarding including network setup and KMS; on-prem longer. we'll open a security checklist and sync with your security team.
[04:16] Janelle Morris: can you send the checklist now?
[04:18] Avery Chen: yes, we'll share the checklist after the call; link to SOC2 and network playbook.
[04:22] [START AUTO SUMMARY INSERT] quick recap: run microbenchmarks, share pricing scenarios, security checklist; follow-up deep dive for VPC. [END AUTO SUMMARY]

[04:35] Marcus Patel: jumping into a quick sample trace — (shares screen) — here's a promo spike: traffic at 4x baseline, long sequences, CPU-bound kernel changes at t+3s causing some token latency. if we enable prefix caching and tune batch window to 20ms we reduce p95 by ~30% in similar runs.
[05:00] Liam O'Connor: how does that batching interact with user-perceived latency on checkout? we need sub-500ms for p95 ideally.
[05:09] Marcus Patel: batching has diminishing returns — smaller windows favor latency, larger windows favor throughput/cost. with KV caching and a 20ms window we see p95 ~420–480ms in our test microbenchmarks for similar workloads.
[05:23] Janelle Morris: that's promising. can Redwood provide recommended defaults we can push into our gateway?
[05:29] Marcus Patel: yes, we'll provide a config snippet for gateway and show how to set routing rules in the console.
[05:34] Rajesh Iyer: what about autoscale cold starts — can we warm caches?
[05:38] Marcus Patel: yes, warmers + pinned KV cache + pre-warming for anticipated promos is recommended. for Dedicated we can also reserve extra capacity for bursts.
[05:48] Priya Singh: a question on logs — retention and PII handling. can we route logs to our SIEM?
[05:54] Sofia Alvarez: yes, audit logs can be exported to your S3 or SIEM and PII redaction rules supported. we'll include the log retention policy in the security packet.
[06:05] Janelle Morris: on adoption — we've rolled features to 12% of users and conversion lift was small but positive; we want to accelerate to 30% without blowing cost. any cost-sparing ideas?
[06:18] Avery Chen: yes — feature flags and progressive rollouts combined with sampling and cached prompts for non-critical flows. Redwood Optimize can suggest quantization and batching profiles per route; typical customers 20–40% token cost reductions with minimal quality impact.
[06:33] Marcus Patel: another lever: use smaller model variant for non-offer-critical queries and route critical checkout calls to higher-quality variant.
[06:42] Rajesh Iyer: can that be automated by route rules?
[06:45] Marcus Patel: yes — console supports per-route model assignments and automatic fallback. we can demo it in the next meeting.
[06:52] Liam O'Connor: are there any hidden costs with prefix cache eviction — e.g., memory usage unexpectedly high?
[06:58] Marcus Patel: cache memory is accounted for in Dedicated sizing; in hosted we manage eviction but will surface cache hit rates. we'll include cache hit rate targets.
[07:08] [08:00] Janelle Morris: (laughs) timeline question — we're planning Black Friday-esque promo in 10 weeks. we need clear runbook and pilot by then.
[07:18] Avery Chen: timeline-wise that's tight but doable: benchmark next week, pilot in 3 weeks, roll to 30% by 6 weeks, full roll by 9–10 weeks if metrics good. we'll put together a 30/60/90 plan.
[07:32] Priya Singh: security review needs to happen earlier — can we do that in parallel?
[07:35] Sofia Alvarez: yes — we'll kick off security assessment immediately after we get your infra diagram.
[07:41] Marcus Patel: small gotcha: if you use product embeddings heavily, we recommend enabling quantization-friendly kernels and checking similarity metrics; some embeddings formats can blow up tokenization.
[07:56] Janelle Morris: we'll send a sample prompt set.
[07:59] Marcus Patel: perfect. also we'll run an A/B test with a quantized variant to measure quality delta.
[08:06] Rajesh Iyer: commercial ask — what's the minimal committed tier for Dedicated?
[08:11] Avery Chen: typical minimum is a 3-month trial at a smaller dedicated pool; we can push a pilot commercial that reduces commit and includes an opt-out if metrics don't meet the SLA. i'll share draft terms.
[08:23] Janelle Morris: price sensitivity: need number for CFO — per-month committed vs expected per-token costs for pilot.
[08:30] Avery Chen: we'll run an expected unit economics sheet tied to your traffic profile — you'll get committed price and projected overages.
[08:36] [09:00] Marcus Patel: quick note on observability — we'll provide per-route dashboards with token-level costs and model-level latency breakdown. that'll help you see hot routes during promos.
[09:12] Liam O'Connor: that dashboard will be helpful for our product managers.
[09:16] Janelle Morris: ok, let's go through open items so we can close the loop.
[09:20] Avery Chen: open items: 1) NexaCart to send infra diagram, traffic profile, and sample prompt set (Priya/Janelle) — due 8/4. 2) Redwood to run microbenchmark plan and share results — target 8/13. 3) Redwood to send security checklist and SOC2/KMS docs — target 8/5. 4) AE to share pilot commercial draft — target 8/6.
[09:44] Priya Singh: confirmed, we'll send diagrams by EOD Monday.
[09:48] Rajesh Iyer: who is point for SRE deep dive?
[09:51] Marcus Patel: Marcus for the SE deep dive; Sofia will coordinate security.
[09:55] Janelle Morris: perfect.
[10:00] Avery Chen: last quick Q: competitors — Rajesh mentioned another vendor ran some numbers for them, anything we should be aware of?
[10:09] Rajesh Iyer: they pitched a cheaper per-token but higher variance in latency. we prefer predictable p95 for checkout.
[10:18] Avery Chen: understood. we'll highlight predictable tail improvements in pilot terms.
[10:22] [11:00] Sofia Alvarez: ok i'm capturing action items in the CSM tracker and will create a follow-up invite for the security deep dive.
[11:08] Janelle Morris: thanks all — appreciate the concrete plan.
[11:12] Avery Chen: thanks everyone — we'll send links to the microbenchmark plan, security docs, and commercial draft after this call. talk soon.

[11:20] (meeting ends)

AUTO-GEN QUESTIONS: 
- "Can Redwood ensure p95 < 500ms during promo bursts?" (short answer: achievable with dedicated/prefix-cache + warmers; need benchmark)
- "How long to onboard VPC/KMS?" (4–8 weeks typical)

REFERENCES SHARED: 
- Microbenchmark plan (link to spreadsheet) — to be sent by Marcus
- Security checklist & SOC2 packet (link) — to be sent by Sofia
- Pilot commercial draft (doc) — to be sent by Avery
